title: Optimal explicit pseudorandom generators for read-once branching programs
formal:
Does there exist one deterministic finite-program algorithm \(A\) and absolute integers \(C,D\ge1\) with the following property? For every \(n,w\ge2\) and \(p\ge1\), all integers, the algorithm specifies an integer seed length \(s=s(n,w,p)\ge0\) and a function
\[G_{n,w,p}:\{0,1\}^{s}\longrightarrow\{0,1\}^{n}\]
with \(s\le Cq\), where \(q=\lceil\log _2 n\rceil+\lceil\log _2 w\rceil+p\), such that every length-\(n\), width-at-most-\(w\) ordered binary read-once branching program \(B\) satisfies
\[\left|\Pr_{u\sim U_s}[B(G_{n,w,p}(u))=1]-\Pr_{z\sim U_n}[B(z)=1]\right|\le 2^{-p}?\]
Here \(U_k\) is the uniform distribution on the \(2^k\) binary strings of length \(k\). Require \(A\) to compute both \(s(n,w,p)\) and any requested bit \(G_{n,w,p}(u)_i\), \(1\le i\le n\), in at most \(Dq\) work bits and \((nw2^p)^D\) steps per call, in the model below. The same algorithm, constants and generator family must work for every parameter triple and every permitted program.
definitions:
A length-\(n\), width-at-most-\(w\) ordered binary read-once branching program consists of nonempty finite layers \(V_0,\ldots,V_n\), each of size at most \(w\), a start state in \(V_0\), an accepting subset of \(V_n\), and functions \(\delta_{i,b}:V_{i-1}\to V_i\) for \(1\le i\le n\), \(b\in\{0,1\}\). On input \(z\), the state is updated by \(\delta_{i,z_i}\) at step \(i\); \(B(z)=1\) exactly when the final state is accepting. The bit order is \(z_1,\ldots,z_n\). Transitions may merge states, including two equally labeled edges from distinct states; no regularity or permutation promise is imposed. The transition tables, start state and accepting subset are arbitrary finite, possibly nonuniform data. The generator receives none of them.

The algorithm is a deterministic multitape Turing machine with a fixed finite program and a mode flag. In the seed-length mode its input is \((n,w,p)\) and its output is \(s(n,w,p)\) in binary. In the bit mode its input is \((n,w,p,u,i)\) and it outputs exactly one bit before halting. Integer parameters use canonical binary notation with separators; the seed is its full binary string, with leading zeroes retained. Inputs occupy read-only tapes whose heads are bounded by endmarkers. There is a fixed finite number of initially blank, semi-infinite work tapes over \(\{0,1,\square\}\), with heads moving by at most one cell per transition. Each distinct work-tape cell visited is charged two work bits, including blank cells. This fixed encoding of tape symbols only fixes a constant in the space bound. All counters, arithmetic, stored history and preprocessing are charged; output is write-only and cannot serve as storage. There is no advice, oracle, external clock or other uncounted memory. Each transition costs one time step. The required bounds hold on every valid call, for every seed and requested index. Only the requested bit must be output in bit mode; there is no requirement to store the whole length-\(n\) string.

Probabilities are exact uniform finite averages. In particular, a seed always has weight \(2^{-s}\), even if several seeds produce the same string; signed weights and externally assigned coefficients are not permitted. The parameter \(p\) controls additive error, not failure probability of a randomized construction: \(A\) itself is deterministic. With \(\varepsilon=2^{-p}\), the target is \(O(\log n+\log w+\log(1/\varepsilon))\) seed length and work space. Ceiling conventions change only constants. Arbitrary \(0<\varepsilon<1\) can be covered by a dyadic tolerance no larger than \(\varepsilon\). No compression requirement \(s<n\) is imposed in parameter regimes where the displayed allowance is already at least \(n\).
answer_criterion: Supply a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the existential proposition above or its full logical negation. An affirmative proof must specify a single finite program and universal constants, formalize its seed-length and bit computations, establish the stated worst-case resource bounds, and prove the additive-error inequality for every permitted program and every parameter triple. A negative proof must rule out every such uniform program and choice of constants; a limitation of one construction, one analysis or one restricted generator class is insufficient. The theorem must use the stated ordinary uniform-seed distribution and arbitrary merging transitions. A result solely for weighted generators, hitting sets or a restricted branching-program subclass does not meet this target.
why: A solution would give a uniform optimal-seed pseudorandom distribution for arbitrary small-memory computations and imply L = BPL. It would close the central gap between the existence of short seeds and their computation in small space, beyond the structural restrictions and weighted approximations covered by current results.

importance.reason: A central constructive route to L=BPL, with optimal nonconstructive seed length known and a persistent gap for uniform space-efficient generators despite advances in restricted and weighted models.

progress.text: Nisan establishes the classical space-bounded PRG construction; the general \(O(\log n\cdot\log(nw/\varepsilon))\) bound is recalled in the inspected 2026 proceedings introduction.
Hoza’s Theorem 1.5 gives weighted seed length \(O(\log(wn)\log n+\log(1/\varepsilon))\), retaining a different output object.
Cheng–Hoza publish the hitting-set implication for two-sided logspace derandomization and the distinct ordinary-PRG parameter connection.
The current Cheng–Wu version retains weighted constructions and explicit restrictions in its regular-program simulation theorem.
Cohen–Doron–Goldgraber state their improved ordinary INW generator under permutation transitions.
The RANDOM proceedings version of Improved Error Reduction for Weighted PRGs is published, retaining the weighted output and the conditional ordinary-PRG implication.
ECCC publishes Krak’s width-three hitting-set preprint; the report’s submission timestamp is 6 September. This is not a claim to the full target.

status_note: Checked on 16 September 2026. The 9 September RANDOM proceedings introduction still identifies the unrestricted ordinary space-efficient PRG target as open. Its new construction is weighted; the July permutation theorem and September width-three hitting-set claim retain additional restrictions or different guarantees. No verified resolution of the complete target was found in the bounded current-source review. New preprint proofs were not independently certified.

context_blocks.text: A branching program models a stream computation that remembers only its current state. Its width \(w\) permits roughly \(\log_2 w\) memory bits, while its length \(n\) counts inspected input bits. The quantifiers require one distribution that works simultaneously for every allowed transition table. Computing a favorable distribution after seeing a particular table would answer a different question.

Short-seed distributions exist nonconstructively; in particular, seed length \(O(\log(n/\varepsilon))\) is known for width-\(n\), length-\(n\) programs. The unresolved issue is explicit computation with the required space bound. An optimal ordinary generator of the kind requested here would imply \(\mathrm L=\mathrm{BPL}\), the equality of deterministic and bounded-error randomized logarithmic-space decision classes. The card does not assert the converse implication.

The classical general bound is \(O(\log n\cdot\log(nw/\varepsilon))\) seed bits. For polynomial width and constant error, this becomes \(O(\log^2 n)\), whereas the requested bound is \(O(\log n)\). The September 2026 RANDOM paper still identifies this general gap, while distinguishing improvements in special width/length regimes.

Weighted generators approximate the acceptance probability by an average \(\mathbb E_u[\rho(u)B(G(u))]\), where \(\rho\) may take negative values. Hoza’s Theorem 1.5 obtains seed length \(O(\log(wn)\log n+\log(1/\varepsilon))\) for this relaxed object. Such weights are useful for deterministic estimates but do not define the ordinary sampled distribution required in this question.

Cheng–Wu’s July 2026 version improves weighted constructions across several parameter regimes. Its optimal-space simulation theorem concerns regular programs in a short-wide regime, not arbitrary programs. A regular program has equal incoming and outgoing degree at each state of each consecutive-layer graph; general transitions in this question can concentrate many incoming edges at one state.

Chen and coauthors improve weighted error reduction and alphabet dependence in the September 2026 proceedings version. Its separate ordinary-generator implication assumes an ordinary PRG with stronger parameter dependence; the weighted theorem does not supply that assumption. The paper credits the earlier Cheng–Hoza result for this connection.

A hitting set guarantees at least one accepting output whenever the uniform acceptance probability exceeds a specified threshold. It need not approximate that probability. Cheng–Hoza prove that a logarithmic-space hitting set for polynomial-width programs would nevertheless imply \(\mathrm L=\mathrm{BPL}\). Their conclusion about class derandomization does not itself produce the ordinary generator required by this card.

For permutation programs, each symbol acts bijectively between consecutive layers of equal size. Cohen–Doron–Goldgraber’s July 2026 theorem gives an ordinary generator with seed \(O((\log w+\log(1/\varepsilon))\log n)\), including arbitrary accepting subsets. The structural promise and remaining product of logarithms distinguish it from the general target.

Krak’s September 2026 preprint states a hitting-set result with seed \(O(\log(n/\varepsilon))\) for ordered width-three programs. The theorem is both a hitting guarantee and a constant-width result; its definition of explicitness requires polynomial time rather than the logarithmic workspace imposed here. This scope review does not independently certify the new proof.

sentences: An ordered read-once branching program reads each input bit in order while retaining one of a bounded number of states, with arbitrary merging transitions allowed.
The question asks for one ordinary uniform-seed generator family that simultaneously approximates the acceptance probability of every such program.
Seed length and worst-case workspace must be linear in the logarithms of length and width plus the error parameter, with a uniform polynomial-in-length,width,inverse-error time bound.
Recent weighted generators, permutation-program PRGs and width-three hitting sets retain guarantees or hypotheses different from this unrestricted target.
A solution requires a complete Lean proof constructing the uniform family with all resource and error bounds, or ruling out every such program and universal constants.

source_formulation.text: The general target is the space-efficient ordinary PRG frontier described in the introduction of Chen et al., RANDOM 2026, and in the earlier Hoza and Cheng–Hoza papers. This card retains its binary, fixed-order, arbitrary-width formulation and the previously stated polynomial-in-\(n,w,1/\varepsilon\) time bound. The explicit tape convention, binary parameters, dyadic errors and uniform constants make that retained target precise; the source papers use asymptotic explicitness conventions.

The historical Nisan PDF could not be retrieved from the listed host (certificate errors locally and HTTP 502 via browser); its bound is supported by this primary discussion and the new 2026 proceedings text, not a claimed fresh reading of the original proof.

Downloaded Cheng–Hoza Theory of Computing 18(21), published 20 September 2022, and read definitions, Theorem 1.3 and Section 4.3 Lemma 4.9 with the preceding error/alphabet discussion. Hitting implies two-sided derandomization under the stated polynomial-width logspace hypothesis; a universal ordinary PRG is a distinct object.

Reused the inspected full Cheng–Wu arXiv:2502.08272v5 dated 10 July 2026: abstract, Definitions 1.1–1.3/1.6, Theorem 1.9 and Section 1.4 Theorem 1.10. These weighted and regular short-program results do not cover the general ordinary PRG target.

New current search found the final RANDOM 2026 publication dated 9 September. Downloaded its full PDF and read the abstract, opening frontier discussion, Theorem 1, Corollary 2, conditional Theorem 3 and Definitions 5–7. Its main improvement is a WPRG; its ordinary-PRG conclusion remains conditional and correctly attributes the earlier connection. The ECCC May revision-specific PDF had also been inspected; its stale root download is not represented as the current version.

Checked current ECCC TR26-123 report with no listed revision and downloaded the full 27-page July PDF. Read introduction, Definitions 2.1–2.3 and Theorem 3.1. The PRG permits any accepting subset but requires both labeled transitions to be permutations. Its seed bound still multiplies log n by log w plus log inverse error.

Checked ECCC TR26-178: submission timestamp 6 September, publication 13 September 2026. Downloaded full PDF and read abstract, Theorem 1.1 and Section 1.4 definitions. The claim is an optimal-seed hitting set for width-three programs; explicit there means polynomial-time output computation, not this card’s workspace guarantee. No complete verification of the new proof is asserted.

Bounded primary-source searches through 16 September 2026 for general optimal read-once branching-program PRGs found the above restricted or weighted advances, not a verified full resolution. No archive bodies were read and no solution to the open problem was attempted.
